blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights the Heard-Of (HO) model as an elegant and unified approach to reasoning about fault-tolerant distributed systems with benign failures. The paper challenges traditional assumptions in distributed computing by modeling systems solely based on transmission failures rather than faulty components, arguing that this simplification leads to clearer and more concise proofs. The key insight is to unify asynchronous and synchronous communication by structuring computations into communication-closed rounds, where missed messages are explicitly modeled as transmission failures. The HO model introduces communication predicates to capture system-specific features and demonstrates its power by deriving conditions for solving consensus and introducing new algorithms like UniformVoting and LastVoting. The model also enables the expression of sporadic conditions, overcoming limitations of augmented asynchronous systems that rely on stable properties.
paper_title: The Heard-Of Model: Computing in Distributed Systems with Benign Failures
paper_abstract: The Heard-Of model is a simple and relatively expressive model of distributed computation. Because of this, it has gained a considerable attention of the verification community. We give a characterization of all algorithms solving consensus in a fragment of this model. The fragment is big enough to cover many prominent consensus algorithms. The characterization is purely syntactic: it is expressed in terms of some conditions on the text of the algorithm. 2012 ACM Subject Classification Theory of computation → Distributed computing models; Software and its engineering → Software verification; Theory of computation → Logic and verification
